input_signals.name: ThinEbitdaCoverageWithDebtBuildup
input_signals.hypothesis: Adding back depreciation to pretax income gives pretax cash earnings, the quantity lenders actually cover; firms whose cash earnings barely cover existing liabilities and who are simultaneously expanding those liabilities are levering into a shrinking cushion and should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This interacts a static coverage-quality state (cash earnings per unit of liabilities, using dp to strip a non-cash charge) with a distress-dynamics channel (one-year liability growth), so neither weak coverage in a stable balance sheet nor debt growth in a well-covered firm scores highly. The mechanism is the ratio of new obligations to servicing capacity, which is economically distinct from the level-based leverage anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( add( pi, dp ), lt ) ) ), rank( growth( lt, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorstYearCashCoverage
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency should be judged at the trough, not the average: the worst annual pretax cash earnings of the last three years relative to total liabilities is a stress-tested coverage measure, and firms whose bad-year cash flow still covers a large share of obligations are far from default and should earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning:
Replacing the tie-heavy 0–3 loss count with the continuous minimum of a cash-earnings series removes the degenerate zero mass while retaining the persistence/severity idea, and it is not the profitability anomaly because two firms with identical average earnings differ sharply in trough earnings. The quality dimension (downside stability of cash generation, using the depreciation add-back) enters through the trough operator and the distress dimension through the liability deflator, so the measure is a single dimensionally coherent default-distance score.
REASONING_NOTE: none
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_min( add( pi, dp ), 3 ), lt ), 1 )

input_signals.name: TroughCoverageFundingGapAdditive
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(TS_MIN(ADD(pi, dp), 3), lt)), RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), act))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency should be judged at the earnings trough rather than the current year, so replacing current cash-earnings coverage with worst-of-three-years coverage inside the winning additive score should sharpen the identification of firms whose funding structure cannot survive a bad year.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates one design choice — the timing/robustness of the coverage leg — within the aggregation form that works, and it is motivated by the fact that trough coverage is the only construct in the archive with an FMB t-stat above 2 in absolute value. If the FMB slope improves on -1.77 while the alpha holds near -5%, downside-state measurement is the right refinement direction for the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( ratio( ts_min( add( pi, dp ), 3 ), lt ) ), ratio( sub( dlc, che ), act ) )

input_signals.name: VolatileTopLineWithFundingGap
input_signals.hypothesis: Demand instability, not just margin instability, determines whether short-term funding can be rolled: a firm whose revenue growth swings violently cannot credibly promise lenders or suppliers the cash flows needed to refinance, so unstable top lines combined with net short-term funding dependence should predict low returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Revenue-growth volatility is a quality dimension the archive has never tested — prior instability legs used margins, coverage or their volatility, all of which mix in cost-side effects — and it is conceptually upstream of both, capturing business-model risk rather than accounting variability. Pairing it additively with the strongest distress leg keeps the structure that has generated joint evidence while introducing genuinely new information.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( vol( growth( revt, 1 ), 3 ), ratio( sub( dlc, che ), act ) )

input_signals.name: FundingGapWithInstabilityAndTroughCoverage
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), act), SUMRANK(VOL(GROWTH(revt, 1), 3), NEG(RATIO(TS_MIN(ADD(pi, dp), 3), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Fragility is the joint product of a withdrawable funding structure, an unpredictable revenue stream, and thin worst-case cash coverage of obligations; the funding gap deserves the largest weight because it is the proximate trigger, while instability and trough coverage each supply independent information about whether a shock will arrive and whether it can be absorbed.
input_signals.reasoning: The nesting deliberately gives the funding gap 50% and the two conditioning channels 25% each, which matches the evidence that the gap is the common leg of the archive's two highest-alpha signals while the instability and trough-coverage legs are the only ones that have delivered |FMB t| above 2. Because the three legs come from the financing mix, the revenue process and the earnings trough, their measurement errors are largely independent, so the composite should improve the cross-sectional slope without giving up the -5% to -6% alpha magnitude.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( dlc, che ), act ), sumrank( vol( growth( revt, 1 ), 3 ), neg( ratio( ts_min( add( pi, dp ), 3 ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FragilityIndexFourLeg
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), act), VOL(GROWTH(revt, 1), 3)), SUMRANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(pi, revt), 3), TS_MIN(RATIO(pi, revt), 3)), NEG(RATIO(TS_MIN(ADD(pi, dp), 3), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distress risk is multidimensional — a withdrawable funding structure, an unpredictable revenue process, asymmetric downside in margins, and thin worst-case coverage of obligations — and an equally weighted index over these four channels should predict returns more reliably than any pair because each channel measures a different failure route.
input_signals.reasoning: The nesting gives each of the four legs exactly 25%, which is the symmetric weighting the critic correctly noted was missing from earlier three-leg attempts, and it unites the archive's FMB-carrying legs (revenue volatility, trough coverage) with its alpha-carrying leg (margin downside asymmetry). Because the legs come from the financing mix, the revenue process, the margin distribution and the earnings trough, their noise is largely independent, so the index should hold the -6% alpha magnitude while lifting the cross-sectional slope past -2.5.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( sumrank( ratio( sub( dlc, che ), act ), vol( growth( revt, 1 ), 3 ) ), sumrank( sub( ma( ratio( pi, revt ), 3 ), ts_min( ratio( pi, revt ), 3 ) ), neg( ratio( ts_min( add( pi, dp ), 3 ), lt ) ) ) )
